hanke_nimi: The role of snowpack and soil freezing in controlling winter season wetland methane emissions (WINMET)
kuvaus: The northern high latitudes have seen increases of mean air temperatures well above the globally documented average, manifested by reductions in snow cover and changes in soil freezing. The wetland methane emissions are closely connected to those changes, however thorough examination of the role of snowpack and soil freezing in controlling the emissions is missing. In this project we will apply versatile field and satellite measurements to study wetland snow and soil properties and greenhouse gas exchange together with atmospheric methane observations. These observations will be used to develop models to further explain the role of the biophysical drivers of the methane emissions and to estimate the regional winter season methane emissions. The aim of the project is to use these diverse methods together to quantify the winter season methane emissions from northern latitude wetlands and to determine the role of snow accumulation and soil freezing in slowing down the emissions. Rahoittaja: Research Council of Finland.

hanke_nimi: The role of soil fauna and biotic interactions in the soil carbon cycling
kuvaus: Soils are the largest reservoirs of terrestrial carbon, thus play a critical role in the global carbon cycling process and consequently in climate regulation. Soils have considerable potential to mitigate climate change through carbon sequestration, thus it is imperative to understand the underlying carbon dynamics mechanisms mediated by the soil biota and their interactions. The importance of soil microbial activities on the soil processes is widely acknowledged, but the impact of soil fauna in carbon dynamics remains poorly quantified. This project aims to quantify the role of soil fauna and their interactions with other soil-inhabiting organisms in the soil carbon cycling processes in boreal forests across Finland. The impact of top-town regulators (soil fauna) on soil microbial activities and community structure will ultimately aid in more accurate predictions about soil carbon dynamics under the changing environmental conditions. Rahoittaja: Research Council of Finland.

hanke_nimi: Unravelling the mechanisms of the soil “microbial carbon pump” – soil C sequestration under global change (UNCAP)
kuvaus: Soils contain twice as much carbon (C) as the atmosphere. Thus, any changes in the rate of release of carbon dioxide (CO2) from soils to the atmosphere can significantly affect climate. Recent methodological advances have revealed that a large part of old, stabilised soil C is derived from dead microbial biomass. In this project, we aim to increase understanding of the mechanisms that affect the fate of this large stable pool of C under climate change. We combine novel stable isotope labelling and compound-specific 13C isotope measurements with experiments that manipulate temperature and nutrient availability along climatic gradients in Northern Europe, Peruvian Andes and the Kenyan highlands, to better understand which factors control stabilisation of microbial derived C. We will assess how changing temperatures and litter inputs affect the balance between increased decomposition of SOM and the stabilization of microbial derived C, in different ecosystems. Rahoittaja: Research Council of Finland.

hanke_nimi: Untangling the role fungal network morphology in soil carbon dynamics
kuvaus: Soils can help mitigating climate change because they can store large amounts of carbon. To realize this potential, we need to include soil fungal diversity (i.e. changes in the number and identity of species present in soil) because these microorganisms transform soil carbon into compounds that alter its persistence. In this project, I develop a new method to measure how fungal diversity impact carbon persistence in soils. The novelty of this project is that it will scale fungal carbon-use traits to fungal network morphology. Soil fungi form networks of interconnected filaments which determine how they use carbon in soils. I use this method to understand carbon persistence in a Finnish boreal forest. Ultimately, this research will help to develop management practices that will enhance the capacity of soils to store carbon and – ideally – mitigate the effects of climate change. Rahoittaja: Research Council of Finland.

hanke_nimi: What are we missing in understanding of soil organic carbon stabilization? Biochemical mechanisms and their significance (BIO-MECH).
kuvaus: Forest ecosystems contain significant amounts of carbon (C) globally, with a major fraction stored belowground, mainly in soil organic matter (SOM). The current conceptual framework of C stabilization is insufficient for the management of SOM pools. This project aims to unravel C stabilization mechanisms and to challenge the current understanding of their role under various forest managements. I propose a novel approach and hypothesize plant-soil-microbe-virus interactions act as key mediators of SOM stabilization. Proposed SOM stabilization mechanisms include a recently unraveled interaction between roots and fungal necromass and two novel mechanisms affecting microbial necromass formation and stabilization: interaction of microbes with viruses and enrichment of root litter with rhizophagy microbes, a group of endophytes. The improved understanding of SOM stabilization mechanisms will inform us how to  increase soil C stabilization through land management to mitigate climate change. Rahoittaja: Research Council of Finland.

hanke_nimi: fun-C: Revealing the links between fungal necromass properties, microbial community composition and soil microbial carbon stocks
kuvaus: Soils are significant reservoirs of carbon(C), and even slight changes in soil respiration have huge impact on the atmospheric CO2 concentrations. As the climate warms, also the soil respiration might increase due to enhanced microbial activity. However, the amount of C allocated to microbial growth might balance out the C lost in soil respiration, and actually the microbial remains contribute significantly to the soil C stocks. Amino sugars(AS) are used as indicators for dead microbial pool in soils since they are part of microbial cell walls. The contribution of fungal cell wall components to soil AS pool is important. Especially melanins, fungal cell wall compounds, contain rather significant amounts of AS, and the fungal hyphae melanin content affects the recalcitrance of the their necromass in soils. The main aim of my project is to find a linkage between native fungal community, especially soil fungal hyphae´s melanin content, and the recalcitrance of microbial remains in soil Rahoittaja: Research Council of Finland.

hanke_nimi: National Soil Greenhouse Gas Test Platform to examine the efficacy of a range of novel fertiliser, bioactives, bio-stimulants, manure, digestate additives.

partnerit: Department of Agriculture Food and the Marine

hanke_nimi: Carbon farming Certification system (CarbFarmS) The transition towards result-based agriculture sector
kuvaus: The overall objective of the “Carbon farming Certification system: The transition towards result-based agriculture sector (CarbFarmS)” project is to develop a roadmap for farmers and decision makers on implementation of Carbon farming Certification system for Latvian conditions, allowing to reach The Green Deal goals in connection with low-carbon circular economy principles. Selected carbon farming solutions and possible result-based payment schemes will be analysed vs its climate, environmental, economic, and social viability. The main aspects to be analysed within the research include: result-based carbon farming schemes, feasibility assessment of proposed solutions, the potential for climate change mitigation. Within the project, carbon farming solutions will be identified, their importance in reducing GHG emissions will be determined and evaluated, indicators for the assessment of solutions will be developed, a risk assessment will be carried out and a roadmap will be developed for the implementation of result-based carbon farming solutions in Latvia. The project is based on consecutive multi-modelling approach combining (1) literature review, (2) indicator analysis method, , (3) multi-criteria descion-making analysis (MCDA), (4) economic analysis and (5)  life cycle assessment (LCA).  ). Combination of the mathematical models deployed in the project will result in a roadmap on carbon farming solutions for Latvia in mid-term and long-term. Rahoittaja: Latvian Council of Science.

hanke_nimi: "Farming carbon" to meet European climate goals: a new market for Swedish forestry?
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: In December 2024 the European Union launched a new voluntary certification framework (CRCF) for carbon removals and hereby initiated a new generation of carbon market activity. The CRCF is part of the EU Green Deal and responds to its overarching goal of turning Europe into the first climate neutral continent by 2050. ‘Carbon farming’ in forests and agricultural lands represents a central source of EU carbon removals and is now launched as a new business model for European landowners. The aim of this project is to critically examine how carbon farming is made thinkable and operable as a domain of EU climate policy and governance, and how it mobilizes the Swedish forestry sector in the European transition to climate neutrality. By analyzing the carbon discourses and practices that underpin the CRCF and 5-8 evolving carbon farming projects in Sweden, Denmark and Finland, the project will assess how carbon farming is enacted in practice and makes Swedish forests governable as a carbon marketplace. Through a combination of document analysis, observations, interviews, and collaborative research activities, the project will compare different carbon farming practices and methodologies that are taking form under the CRCF and give guidance on how Swedish forest owners can be sustainably engaged in the European race to net-zero emissions.  Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Can reduced soil tillage mitigate nitrogen losses and increase carbon sequestration in arable cropping systems?
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – null
kuvaus: Soil systems play an important role in the global fluxes of greenhouse gases (GHGs), especially of carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide (N2O) and their carbon and nitrogen cycles are tightly connected. Soil tillage in agricultural systems is a central factor in determining the net contribution of GHGs, but also in determining soil organic carbon sequestration, risk of soil erosion, soil fertility, nutrient leaching, decomposition of pesticides, water quality and infiltration, fossil energy consumption and crop yields. It is hypothesized that soil tillage enhanced carbon sequestration have significant effects on nitrogen use and losses in agroecosystems. Consequently, it is essential to understand these relationships to be able to counterbalance unwanted effects. The objectives of this study is to determine the effect of a shift from conventional tillage using ploughing to reduced (shallow) tillage with only surface incorporation of crop residues during 18 years on the emission of N2O, the recovery (and loss) of 15N-labelled nitrogen fertilizer in crops and soil, the soil organic carbon sequestration in the profile, the soil physical quality parameters and crop yields within a diverse (6-yrs) arable crop rotation. The project will result in new valuable knowledge on the possibilities for increasing the sustainability of cropping system via reduced soil tillage. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Carbon Farming Living Labs
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Governmental Agency for Innovation Systems – Project grant
kuvaus:
Purpose and goal:
Within the project, we built an international consortium. Together we prepared and submitted an application to the Horizon Europe Mission´s ´A Soil Deal for Europe´ call for Carbon Farming Living Labs.

Expected results and effects:
We built a consortium with leading international institutes within the subject area. We developed and submitted a competitive project application. We hope that the Horizon Europe project will be granted.

Approach and implementation:
Together with our project partners, we carried out intensive networking during the early project phase to build a consortium. The consortium then developed a suitable project concept, wrote and submitted a competitive project proposal. The consortium was updated and adapted to the project needs throughout the development phase. Rahoittaja: Swedish Governmental Agency for Innovation Systems.

hanke_nimi: Carbon farming as a climate measure: a farmer perspective
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: Carbon farming is increasingly promoted as a solution to transform the agricultural sector’s relationship to climate change and as a strategy to reach net-zero emissions targets. But despite the potential of soils to act as a carbon sink, the effectiveness of carbon farming as a climate measure is conditioned by whether farmers are willing and able to change their everyday practices and the overall impacts on farming systems and livelihoods. Drawing on place-based, empirically grounded research, the overall aim of this research project is therefore to evaluate the potential of carbon farming to act as a climate measure, with focus on the farmer perspective. We thereby seek to address the gap in engagement with producer perspectives in soil carbon research. We will identify farmers’ incentives and barriers to engage in carbon farming, and how these may affect different groups of producers. Furthermore, we will assess potential synergies, trade-offs and tensions associated with carbon farming as a climate measure in relation to other social-environmental goals. In short, we ask: what is in it for the farmer? Based on interaction with key stakeholders, a second aim of the project is to identify current gaps and needs, as well as options for policy and governance measures that could support the promotion of carbon farming. We thereby seek to combine critical and solutions-oriented research in support of a broader transition of agricultural systems towards sustainability. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Does nutrient limitation promote carbon storage in forest soils?
kuvaus: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is a major component of the global carbon (C) cycle. Its vulnerability to disturbances and climate variations has been studied, but its response to altered nutrient availability is not well known. Nitrogen (N) in particular is fundamental for the microbes that mediate the degradation of SOC, so that changes in N availability can alter the SOC balance. Three microbial responses to N shortage are hypothesized: HP1) enzyme synthesis is slowed down, thus reducing C emissions; HP2) the efficiency of conversion of C into biomass (C-use efficiency, CUE) is reduced, which would maintain or increase C emissions; HP3) microbial internal recycling of N is increased. Here we start by focusing on decomposition and ask: Q1) Which of these mechanisms is dominant, and what is their combined net effect on SOC? We will then scale up to the ecosystem level, including plant-symbiont interactions, to ask: Q2) How does N limitation interplay with plant-microbe-soil interactions (priming)? To this aim, we will harmonize existing stoichiometric theories under a common framework that accounts for all these different mechanisms, and synthesize literature data from microbial isolates to field scale, leveraging national soil surveys. Theoretical explorations and meta-analyses will allow answering our questions, and specifically assessing the consequences of N addition (deposition, fertilization) and limitation (due to higher atmospheric CO2) on SOC stocks in forests. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: Ectomycorrhizal fungi as drivers for iron-mediated oxidation of soil organic matter
kuvaus: Oxidative decomposition of soil organic matter (SOM) determines the fraction of carbon that is either stored or emitted into the atmosphere as CO2. Current models attribute this oxidation largely to the activity of extracellular enzymes. However, recent studies suggest that non-enzymatic processes including the action of reactive oxygen (ROS) species generated by Fenton-like reactions at the surface of redox active iron containing minerals contribute significantly to oxidative decomposition of SOM. Organic and mineral soil layers of boreal forest are rich in iron oxides. Ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungi often dominate the microbial biomass in these environments. The aim of this four-year project is to examine the capacity of ECM fungi of diverse ecologies and evolutionary histories to induce ROS and oxidize SOM associated with iron oxides. We will examine the mechanisms by which these fungi produce ROS using laboratory-scale systems combined with isotopic, spectroscopic and chromatographic methods. We will use experiments and dynamic modelling to determine the main environmental and biological regulators controlling the production of ROS. This is an interdisciplinary project involving competences in microbial ecology, molecular geochemistry and systems biology. If the capacity to induce Fenton-like reactions at mineral surfaces is widespread among ECM fungi, the role of these fungi in soil C cycling may be much more important than currently considered. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: Effects of soil organic carbon fractions on soil structure and preferential solute transport
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: Carbon sequestration in arable soils has been described as a ‘win-win’ strategy to mitigate climate change and restore the productive capacity of degraded agricultural land. Soil organic carbon (SOC) is intimately linked to soil structure which in turn largely determines solute transport through soil. The objective of this project is to quantify the effects of different SOC fractions on soil structural pore space and preferential solute transport in Swedish agricultural topsoils. To achieve this, we will relate the characteristics of the soil structural pore space determined by X-ray tomography to measurements of functional SOC pools and non-reactive solute transport quantified in column experiments. Results will be analyzed in relation to soil carbon saturation (i.e. ratio of clay to SOC). The project consists of two parts: (1) a study at the field scale, where it can be assumed that only basic soil properties such as texture and organic matter content vary between sampling locations, and (2) a regional scale study where other factors affecting soil structure, such as climate, management practices and clay mineralogy may also vary. This project will demonstrate the extent to which increases in soil organic matter content will also reduce pollutant losses to water. This quite unrecognized additional benefit of carbon sequestration should provide further impetus to policies aimed at encouraging management practices that promote carbon sequestration in arable soil. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Effects of stump and slash harvesting on soil carbon and nutrient pools
ohjelmakausi: The Swedish Energy Agency – Project grant
kuvaus: This project is part of the overarching project Effects of tree-stump harvest on soil, water and climate. The project investigates effects of stump and slash harvesting on soil carbon and nutrient pools, including soil acid-base status in 9 field trials, approx. 30 years after harvesting. In a corresponding way, the project also examines the soils of 12 new field experiments to be established in Sweden. For the first purpose, we use the SLU study sites established by Lars Kardell, where soil studies have not previously been made. The aim of the second part of the project is to document site conditions just prior to stump harvesting in order to improve the scientific value of the trials. In the new experiments, initial treatment effects on soil carbon dioxide emissions will be made, including a pilot study on N2O and methane emissions. Rahoittaja: The Swedish Energy Agency.

hanke_nimi: Feeling the heat(h): Can reindeer grazing stabilize soil organic matter in arctic and alpine tundra heath under climate warming?
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Grant for positions or stipends
kuvaus: Plants, microbes, and their interactions determine soil carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling and stocks. Climate warming is shifting plant and microbial communities in arctic and subarctic tundra, potentially altering ecosystem services and the livelihood of indigenous peoples. Reindeer grazing may regulate these changes by preventing tree and shrub expansion and by influencing soil N availability and microbial functioning.This project aims to understand how reindeer grazing interacts with soil C and N cycling in tundra ecosystems, and how related ecosystem services are affected along a gradient of reindeer grazing intensity. I will use a unique set of soils collected within and outside of long-term reindeer exclosures in 20 areas distributed across the Arctic. Firstly, I will quantify the global importance of grazing intensity for soil C and N stocks in relation to vegetation, soil, microbial and climatic factors. Secondly, I will characterize mechanisms underlying soil organic matter stability in tundra heath in a litter bag experiment. Thirdly, I will study reindeer grazing effects on these mechanisms and on ecosystem services provided by soils, particularly soil C sequestration and regulation of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.This research should unravel the drivers of soil C and N cycling in grazed tundra and support decision makings on land-use to promote optimal grazer management that enhances soil C storage and reduces GHG emissions.  Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Improved estimation and mitigation of nitrous oxide emissions and soil carbon storage from crop residues
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: Crop residues provide large inputs of carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) to soils and contribute to the net GHG balance of soils in different ways.They are included as a key component in national emissions inventories for nitrous oxide (N2O) from agriculture. Residue are also a majorcontributor to sustaining or enhancing soil organic carbon (SOC) and N contents and thus soil fertility. Depending on the amount of C and Nin crop residues and their contributions to N2O emissions or to the SOC balance residues might increase or decrease the GHG footprint ofagroecosystems.Studies have shown that N2O emissions from N in crop residues vary considerably depending on residue quality, residue management andsoils. This is currently not reflected in emissions inventories or likely not sufficiently in simulation models. This makes current emissioninventories uncertain and in many cases biased. Lack of knowledge and precise model estimation of N2O emissions and SOC storage fromcrop residues limits the design of improved crop management systems for net GHG emissions reductions.ResidueGas will document an improved methodology to quantify N2O emissions from agricultural crop residues management, includingstandards for estimating the amount of N in residues and improved emission factors for crop residue that include effects of residue quality,management, soils and climate on emissions. ResidueGas will further identify and communicate best practice for crop residue managementstrategies with respect to their net greenhouse gas effect in terms of N2O emissions and SOC storage.The transnational team in ResidueGas has the necessary breadth of high-level expertise to undertake the task, covering knowledge onrelevant cropping systems, measurements of GHG emissions (N2O) and SOC at both field and lab scales, access to existing data on cropresidues and emissions, expertise in biogeochemical modelling of GHG emissions and knowledge on GHG inventory reporting at farm andnational scale. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Is boreal soil carbon getting younger? Using historical samples to advance predictions of soil carbon sinks under rising atmospheric CO2
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council – Grant for positions or stipends
kuvaus: Boreal soils constitute the largest global organic carbon pool with a strong CO2 sink strength. However, the quantitative prediction of how this sink strength will change under increasing atmospheric CO2 concentration remains highly uncertain. Addressing this gap necessitates the development of effective modelling approaches.Using historical samples from intensive soil nitrogen manipulation experiments and an extensive soil sample archive at the national scale collected between 1980’s and 2022, and advanced computational modelling, the overarching objective of the project is to advance our understanding of how boreal carbon sinks respond to rising CO2 and soil nitrogen conditions, with a particular focus on the carbon transit time and the chemical compositions of soil organic matter. Over this period, CO2 levels rose from 340 to 420 ppm, while the signature of atmospheric ∆14C decreased from 200‰ to 0‰, providing distinct annual ∆14C signatures of the carbon input to the soil. By integrating estimated carbon transit time of soil organic matter with stable isotopic data (13C and 15N) and pyrolysis-GC-MS and 13C-NMR analyses, I expect to provide essential parameters to constrain current Earth system models.Given the originality of the research question and the innovative modelling tools, this project is expected to make a significant impact in the field of soil science, biogeochemical modelling, and climate projection. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: Muddy terrains of environmental expertise: Ethnographies of changing and competing knowledge of wetland restoration in times of climate change
kuvaus: Freshwater is an increasingly acute issue for cities in the context of the multifaceted climate crisis. In response to this, restoration of freshwater urban ecosystems is gaining momentum. However, restoration is far from straightforward, as diverse ways of knowing, valuing and living with ecosystems are at stake in claims about imperatives for their remaking on the ground. By investigating the multiplicity, diversity and ordering of expertise that inform urban restoration, this project seeks to identify dominant knowledge regimes, value conflicts and local ecosystem understandings that underpin contemporary ecosystem restoration. It does so by addressing the overall research question: How is dominant restoration expertise constructed and maintained? Wetland restoration in Stockholm (Sweden) is the empirical entry point for ethnographic studies of urban restoration expertise in the making. Across three years, the project charts the local, social and material contingencies through which such expertise is produced, and informs restoration action, and inaction. Key methods are walking interviews with professionals involved in municipal restoration interventions, and observations and interviews at national policy events gathering urban water expertise. Ultimately, the project contributes with insights into which modes of urban ecosystem restoration that are gaining prominence, and the alternatives of urban water futures that by these are foreclosed and marginalized.   Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: Prime time in the rhizosphere - Mobilization of mineral-protected organic matter at the root-soil interface
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council – Grant for positions or stipends
kuvaus: Root-soil interactions lie at the heart of the soil carbon (C) and nutrient balances, but uncertainties about these interactions hamper projections of soil-climate feedbacks. To date, most studies of root-induced C losses have focused on microbial aspects, assuming that root exudates accelerate microbial activity and thus turnover of ‘old’ organic matter. But, up to 90% of a soil’s C inventory is associated with minerals, preventing microbial access. This project aims to evaluate exudate-induced mechanisms mobilizing mineral-protected organic matter by transforming mineral-organic associations (MOAs). The main hypothesis is that roots release ligands and reductants which attack the integral building blocks of MOAs. The experimental design allows access to root-soil interfaces of growing roots. Novel optical sensors and microdialysis will be used to define geochemical controls on MOA stability. Most vulnerable MOAs and C forms will be identified by synchrotron-based X-ray absorption spectroscopy and microscopy, while an innovative dual-isotope approach will quantify fluxes of C. The project combines two-years of research at University of Massachusetts Amherst and Stanford University, USA, with one year at Lund University. Its outcome will advance our mechanistic understanding of organic matter dynamics in soils and contribute to ongoing work at the host institutions to improve terrestrial C models. Thus, it improves our ability to project soil feedbacks to the climate system. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: Root decomposition important in comparison of carbon balances after stump harvest and soil scarification
ohjelmakausi: The Swedish Energy Agency – Project grant
kuvaus:
This project contributes to a better understanding of the climate characteristics of stumps by clarifying what the decomposition rate of roots means for both stumps’ direct climate effects, taking into account the time frame as for the indirect effects of stump harvesting on forest soil carbon storage. The project is a continuation of a new project with the same name which is ongoing in 2012. If the decomposition rate of the roots is shown to be significant, this may justify the continuation of the project during 2013-2015 with the aim of improving the valuation of the climate characteristics of stumps under different conditions and harvesting techniques.  

The continuation of the project has been tentatively budgeted with funding from the Swedish Energy Agency, SLU and forestry sector.

Definitive assessment of this application may, in light of the above, not take place before we have the results of the first year, 2012. We hope, however, on a preliminary assessment. I ask that the application be deferred to the end of the year, when I come back with the results of the first year. Rahoittaja: The Swedish Energy Agency.

hanke_nimi: Site preparation and bioenergy harvest: How is the carbon stock in soil and biomass affected after 10 years?
ohjelmakausi: The Swedish Energy Agency – Project grant
kuvaus: Site preparation promotes tree growth and increases carbon storage in tree biomass. Extraction of bioenergy from the forest, such as slash and stumps, increases removal of biomass carbon after harvesting. Both measures aim to counteracting climate change, if they do not lead to significant loss of soil carbon, which is a common concern for site preparation and bioenergy harvest. In this project, we investigate how the carbon stock in soil and biomass is affected by site preparation and slash and stump harvesting during the clear-cut and young forest phase. We investigate fourteen experiments located across Sweden in the project. Modelling effect of slash and stump extraction on carbon balance is a supplement to the field investigation. Finally, a knowledge synthesis is carried out, aimed at stakeholders of forests and forestry in Sweden. The synthesis describes how the carbon stocks in soils are affected by site preparation and bioenergy harvest under Swedish conditions. Rahoittaja: The Swedish Energy Agency.

hanke_nimi: Soil organic matter dynamics in boreal forests  – the role of mycorrhizal mycelia and microbial communities
kuvaus: Chemical and biological mechanisms underpinning long-term soil carbon storage in boreal forests are poorly known, but a high proportion of stable soil organic matter (SOM) consists of microbial residues. The aim is to increase our understanding of how ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungal mycelia and associated microbial communities contribute to long-term stable SOM formation. The 4-year project is organised in three parts focusing on 1) mycelial decomposition under varying growth conditions, 2) investigations of the chemical quality and community composition of in situ mycelial communities, and 3) quantification of SOM fractions and their associated microbial communities and functions. We make use of environmental gradients to perform experiments testing how decomposition is affected by fungal traits and environmental conditions, and we collect composite mycelial samples by incubating sand-filled in-growth mesh bags in situ. Methods include chemical characterization of mycelia using Fourier Transform Infra-Red spectroscopy, SOM fractionations, visualization and elemental analysis using SEM, together with quantification and meta-barcoding of microbial communities, and activity measurements (e.g. enzyme activities). The project will contribute to the fundamental understanding of links between microbial phylogenetic and functional biodiversity, and SOM dynamics, motivated by a lack of in-depth mechanistic understanding of SOM transformations, and the role of soil microbial communities.  Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: Swedish Carbon Sequestration, collaboration within the food system for increased carbon farming in Sweden
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Governmental Agency for Innovation Systems – Project grant
kuvaus:
Purpose and goal:
The aim of the project is to reduce carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere through a transformation of Swedish agriculture. We have launched a prototype of a platform that brings together businesses that want to pay for carbon sequestration with farmers who implement carbon sequestering and soil improvement measures. It has been developed in collaboration with over 70 stakeholders to meet a wide range of needs, and it is aligned with international standards.

Expected results and effects:
Carbon sequestration methods have been applied to 42 pilot farms, different methods for measuring sequestered carbon have been tested and are used in calculation models for carbon sequestration. The platform prototype has been launched and is in use, knowledge dissemination and advice are requested and ongoing. Swedish companies, not just the food sector, are showing interest in investments in Swedish agriculture. Svensk Kolinlagring is a trusted partner by various actors: farmers, researchers, authorities, advisors and investing businesses.

Approach and implementation:
Through the work packages TEST, BUILD, THINK, PROTOTYPE, WORLD and LEAD, we have collaborated and developed our platform. We have worked with technical development, education, networking, measurements, calculations, business intelligence, lectures, farm visits and workshops. Relationship building is key, we place great emphasis on creating a good collaborative climate - thanks to good relationships, we were able to take the step to launch, despite uncertainties and risks. Rahoittaja: Swedish Governmental Agency for Innovation Systems.

hanke_nimi: The Future of LULUCF and REDD+ in the Post-Kyoto Framework
ohjelmakausi: The Swedish Energy Agency – Project grant
kuvaus: Can forests play a more meaningful role in the general international climate policy framework? This question is currently being asked at multiple levels: at the EU level, in the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change’s Kyoto and Post Kyoto frameworks, including with respect to the development of REDD+ approaches that attempt to reduce the rate of deforestation and forest degradation in the developing world. The parallel evolution of the REDD+ framework in particular poses one additional question: are the emerging Annex I and non-Annex I policy frameworks compatible? Can they help promote and fulfill common goals? In addition to a broader range of ecosystem services, forests are important stores of carbon as well as important contributors to the hydrologic cycle and to biodiversity. Thus strategies that preserve and promote the world’s forests naturally help promote the goals of climate change mitigation and potentially also adaptation. In order to integrate forests more firmly into the international climate policy framework, more efficient and precise monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) strategies must be developed and spread evenly across all participating countries. Rahoittaja: The Swedish Energy Agency.

hanke_nimi: The fate of organic carbon in small mountain rivers in the Himalayas: Implications for soil erosion and climate change
kuvaus: Certain natural processes and land-use practices accelerate the disturbance of soil organic carbon (OC). This is a large problem in mountainous terrains, where small mountain rivers (SMR) erode and transport OC-rich top soil. A large amount of this OC pool in SMRs represents highly aged C, which when oxidized can be an additional hidden source of greenhouse-gas emission. OC release and oxidation via this aquatic conduit poses a livelihood challenge because loss of soil-OC diminishes its quality for agriculture, and degradation of OC could affect the climate. Nepal is affected by these changes both on short and long-term scales. Hence, the overarching aims of this study are to 1) develop and implement novel approaches to quantify the spatial and temporal variability of OC flux, and its fate in SMRs, and 2) initiate awareness and specific outreach activities for sustainable development practices. We will implement these goals by studying the variation of well-established multi-proxy physical and geochemical parameters in two SMRs located in western Nepal. The project will support proactive research initiatives and communication, and two-way knowledge exchange. These efforts will contribute towards better synergy, filling in knowledge gaps, and provide data for launching better soil conservation efforts and land-use practices. Moreover, it will empower the local community in making suitable and judicious decisions for sustainable development practices and reduce poverty. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: The metabolic age of soil organic matter
kuvaus: The composition and fate of soil organic carbon are of uttermost importance for soil properties and long-term soil fertility. Also, the contemporary global soil carbon pool stores three times the amount of atmospheric CO2-C and is thereby a most important potential atmospheric CO2 source.  Despite a century-long scientific effort, several fundamental properties of soil organic matter (SOM) are still unresolved. One of the most striking paradoxes is that O-alkyl and di-O-alkyl carbons are prominent forms of SOM irrespective of soil type. These carbon forms are interpreted as constituents of carbohydrate polymers, e.g. cellulose and hemicelluloses, and should therefore be absent from old soils.  The research proposal builds on the idea that intramolecular distributions of stable heavy isotopes (ISOTOPOMERS) can give fundamentally new information, because their abundances directly reflect isotope fractionation by biochemical processes. Our central objective is to demonstrate the potential of isotopomers to trace carbon turnover in soils. The project focuses on two hypotheses: 1) Isotopomer abundances can be used to identify compound-specific turnover pathways of soil organic matter; 2) Compounds that APPEAR as retained ("recalcitrant") in soils can have been recycled multiple times with increasing soil age. This turnover causes progressive changes in isotopomer patterns, which therefore are indicative of the "metabolic age" of these compounds. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council.

hanke_nimi: The two-way interactions between soil organic carbon and soil structure
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: Well-developed soil structure (i.e. the spatial arrangement of solids and pores) is critical for sustainable crop production. Soil structure is largely influenced by aggregation induced by the microbial decomposition of organic matter. In turn, soil structure affects soil organic matter (SOM) turnover because pore networks determine microbial access to SOM and the oxygen supply to soil microbes. These two-way interactions between soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil structure have recently been included in SOC turnover models. Suchmodels are important tools to analyse the effects of soil and crop management practices and climate change on SOC stocks. However, it is not clear what determines the amount of aggregation created by SOC and how efficiently this aggregation protects SOM from degradation.To establish relations between SOC, soil structure formation and SOC protection for Swedish soils and climate we will quantify soil structure using X-ray tomography and measure SOC contents and respiration on intact soil aggregates sampled from long-term field experiments. We will also quantify the formation of soil structure during incubation experiments using sieved soil, organic amendments and reactive aluminium phases. The results from this project will provide new guidance on model parameterisation and facilitate more climate-smart agricultural management where investments to enhance carbon sequestration are directed to the soils where they will be most efficient. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: The unaccounted nitrous oxide reducing microbial community: a nitrous oxide sink in agricultural soils
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – null
kuvaus: The aim is to identify soil factors and ecological processes that drive activity and assembly of microbial communities that reduce the greenhouse gas N2O in arable soil. A recent discovery shows that N2O reducers are an unaccounted resource for lowering N2O emissions. A better understanding their ecology integrated with knowledge within precision agriculture has potential to accommodate measures in agricultural for mitigation of N2O emissions. First, we will use a novel approach that combine a phylogenetic and ecological framework with geostatistical modeling to provide insights into the relative importance of evolutionary and ecological forces structuring N2O reducing communities in space. Predicting spatial patterns at the field scale is the first step in identifying the resource-based habitat of these communities at a scale compatible with land management. These patterns will generate hypotheses that we will test in experiments to determine the causal effects of soil factors and ecological processes on assembly of N2O reducers and how that affects N2O reduction and net N2O emissions. We will use a novel 15N method and soils that allow us to also link the results from the experiments to in situ N2O fluxes. Increased knowledge of factors promoting soil N2O reducers and their activity is essential to undertake proper actions for N management in agriculture and improve the terrestrial climate regulation service. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Tillage effects on soil organic carbon and phosphorus stratification and storage in Swedish soils
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – null
kuvaus: Conventional tillage in Sweden comprises stubble cultivation, ploughing and seedbed preparation. This system can be replaced by reduced tillage (cultivation to shallower depths) or direct drilling (sowing without prior loosening of the soil). Conventional tillage homogenizes the soil and evenly distributes soil organic carbon (SOC) and phosphorus (P) in the ploughing layer, while reduced tillage or direct drilling stratifies them with more accumulation near soil surface. The aim of this project is to evaluate tillage impacts on the stratification and accumulation of SOC and P in Swedish long-term tillage experiments under conventional vs. reduced tillage. The final goal is to propose soil tillage strategies, which can enhance carbon sequestration with minimum risks for phosphorus losses. We assume that continuous reduced tillage or direct drilling does not necessarily lead to increased carbon stock when considering the whole soil profile. We also assume that continuous reduced tillage or direct drilling accumulates P near soil surface, which may pose P losses via runoff & leaching. Investigation will be carried out in 6 long-term experiments. SOC and P will be determined in various layers, totally to 50 cm soil depth. Soil macropore structure and leaching risks for P will be investigated by dye tracing and rain simulation, respectively. The project will have high values for the society with respect climate (carbon sequestration) and eutrophication (P losses to water bodies). Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Turnover of organic matter in agricultural soil throughout the year
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: Soil organic matter (SOM) is one of the most important determinants for soil fertility and key ecosystem services SOM controls soil structure, water holding capacity and nutrient delivery; but is also important for the sequestration of atmospheric CO2. In agricultural soils, management of plant residues and the use of fertilisers are governing SOM balances, but mechanisms and controls are far from fully understood. Recent studies have shown that the microbial community composition has a profound impact on SOM turnover. In the proposed project, we aim at investigating how much of the old organic matter in agricultural soils is decomposed by microbes, and how much of new plant material that is converted to stabilised humus, as an effect of different fertiliser strategies. New technologies will be used, combining analysis of stable isotopes (13C/12C) in soil respiration and in PLFAs (phospholipid fatty acids) in microbes with molecular biology methods. This will give a better understanding of SOM dynamics in the agricultural ecosystem. The project will have a direct impact on the national reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and will provide a scientific basis for policy instruments aiming at management practices for increasing soil fertility and carbon sequestration. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: Using wetland restoration as a tool to mitigate runoff extremes
ohjelmakausi: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning – Project grant
kuvaus: Restoration of drained wetlands to more pristine conditions is considered as one of the most important strategies to avoid catastrophic effects of extreme weather. This includes avoiding both flooding during large precipitation events and streams from drying out during droughts. However, the science underpinning this strategy is largely missing, and in fact, the few scientific studies of pristine wetland systems in Sweden do not support the notion that wetland restoration necessarily is the best strategy to reduce extreme weather impacts. To overcome this lack of scientific arguments and to close the gap between science and management, we will utilize a unique collection of hydrological field observations and modelling to address the question whether restored wetlands are more effective in mitigating both flooding events and low flow conditions than leaving historically drained wetlands as they are. To do this, our multi-sectorial team will take full advantage of one of the most advanced field research infrastructures, the Krycklan Catchment Study (KCS, www.slu.se/Krycklan). By combining data from KCS with a state-of-the-art methodology for estimating water storage and release dynamics, we will be able to evaluate and compare the role of i) pristine wetlands without drainage, ii) historically drained wetlands carried out in the 1930s to improve forest productivity, iii) newly ditched-cleaned wetlands for forestry production and, iv) recently restored wetlands. Rahoittaja: Swedish Research Council for Environment, Agricultural Sciences and Spatial Planning.

hanke_nimi: WP1 - Bioenergy and links to agriculture and LULUCF in a Nordic context
ohjelmakausi: The Swedish Energy Agency – Project grant
kuvaus: The overall aim of the project is to contribute to and increase the knowledge and understanding of mechanisms that affect the biomass potential in the Nordic energy system and investigate how the environmental impact of agriculture-based bioenergy can be assessed using different calculation frameworks. Main targets are to identify key aspects affecting the biomass potential from agriculture and the resulting GHG emissions of using the biomass in the energy system, and to investigate how updated scenarios for agricultural biomass potential can be integrated into the Open Nordic TIMES model. The Swedish Energy Agency assesses that the project has the potential to contribute to the call's goals. Rahoittaja: The Swedish Energy Agency.
